summary: The help file for the Utah-10 implementation of the user FTP process, offered as the only documentation produced so far. It covers control characters and gives a detailed command listing.

plainLanguage.summary: A help sheet for a file-sending program, listing the keys and commands you can press.

subtitle: Help documentation for the Utah-10 user FTP process

tldr.problem: No formal documentation exists for the Utah-10 FTP user interface, making it hard for users to learn the command language.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC reproduces the help file that appears when a user types HELP, covering control characters, general information, command syntax and detailed command descriptions.
tldr.outcome: Users have a reference for how to use the FTP interface, including how to transfer, rename and delete files.

today: RFC 412 provided documentation for a specific FTP implementation in 1972. It has not been updated or superseded, though FTP itself has evolved.

sections.title: What Is This Documentation
sections.content: RFC 412 is the help file from the Utah-10 implementation of a user FTP process. It is the only documentation produced to date for this interface. The FTP user process simplifies transferring files between hosts on ARPANET by providing a natural command language designed to be easy to learn.
sections.plainLanguage: This is a user manual for a program that transfers files between computers. It explains what commands you can type.

sections.title: Control Characters and Editing
sections.content: The interface uses several control characters: Control-Z aborts the current command. For editing, Control-A and Control-H delete a character, Control-W deletes a word (or the entire line for certain functions), and Control-V treats the next character literally. Alt-Mode (ESC) terminates a command and shows suggestions; Control-X and Rub-Out abort. Control-R retypes the line. The ? character provides command completion and lists available commands.
sections.plainLanguage: Special keys on your keyboard do things like delete text or get help, just like on other computers.

sections.title: Basic Commands and File Operations
sections.content: Key commands include connecting to a host by name or number; RETRIEVE or GET downloads a remote file; STORE or SEND uploads a file; APPEND adds to a remote file; RENAME and DELETE work on remote files. BYE ends the session with the remote server. MODE sets transfer format: STREAM for raw bit stream (default), BLOCK for formatted blocks, TEXT for text mode using Telnet codes, or HASP for compressed data. TYPE and BYTE set encoding; STRUCTURE defines file organization.
sections.plainLanguage: You can type commands to connect to another computer, download or upload files, rename things, and set how data is formatted when sent.
